column3: Persisted token values remain opaque strings and token_type, rather than provider-specific string shape, determines whether a token is ETag, generation, or emulated
The v3 cas_blob header occupies exactly 256 bytes: JSON occupies [0,json_len), spaces occupy [json_len,255), and byte 255 is a newline
The v3 cas_blob tag is a fresh random u128 per upload attempt and is the exact-token delete primitive; bld attributes newborn debris to the writer build
The v3 cas_blob envelope retains constant payload offset blob_header_len = 256 and does not use frame-level compression because payload identity is the raw bytes
Provider metadata is only a mirror for eyes and dashboards; the CAS protocol never reads it and must fail closed if it is absent
RustFS has demonstrably returned incomplete LIST results, while AWS S3 was untested in the cited investigation; correctness cannot rely on assumed store LIST behavior.
Freshness metadata is advisory: writers may point-read per-hash `.meta`, but reads do not consult it, GC deletes the blob body first, and an absent meta is equivalent to `Clean`.
Mutable and control protobuf objects should use `CasHeader`; streamed blob payloads should keep a binary envelope, and GC data-plane runs should use `RunFile`.
CAS blobs and manifests are immutable, content-addressed, write-once objects, and GC is required to preserve no dangle, no returned token, and over-count rather than under-count.
Persisted `BlobRef` fields use `ha` for the hash algorithm and `h` for the digest hex, and the searched user-facing tools contain no `p` JSON/output key.
Setting `metadata_type` to `cas` makes an object-storage disk content-addressed, shares identical content across parts or tables, and enables background reclamation after references disappear.
CAS integration configs use `<metadata_type>cas</metadata_type>` and the relink test asserts the wire literals `cas_pool_uuid`, `cas_relink=part_manifest_v2`, and `cas_source_token`.
`uploadPendingBlobs` creates one `Cas::BlobUploadRequest` per referenced pending blob and delegates to the free function `DB::Cas::fanOutBlobUploads(build, requests, pool, hooks=nullptr)`.

Fan-out tasks write only their own pre-sized stable result slot; the runner is declared after the result vector so its destructor drains every task before the vector is destroyed, including a dispatch-loop throw (`B90`).
`waitForAllToFinishAndRethrowFirstError` drains all tasks and then rethrows the first failure in ascending-ref order, and a rethrow bypasses merging results.
Duplicate blob references collapse to one upload task, and conflicting duplicate declared sizes are rejected with `LOGICAL_ERROR`.
Fan-out concurrency is bounded by the supplied pool size: pool 2 reaches peak concurrency 2, while pool 1 degenerates to serial execution with a bounded wait.
`clickhouse-local` initializes the blob-upload pool from `content_addressed_blob_upload_pool_size` during `LocalServer::initialize` and shuts it down during `LocalServer::cleanup`.
`clickhouse-disks` initializes the blob-upload pool with `DB::Cas::initializeBlobUploadPool(16)` and shuts it down in its existing `SCOPE_EXIT_SAFE` block.
The generation-8 canonical snapshot wire remains byte-identical, retains mandatory `"lc":"live"`, and does not bump `G_BUILD`.
Snapshot encoding writes literal `lc = live`; decoding requires the `lc` field and accepts exactly `live`.
Generation-8 snapshot decoding explicitly rejects retired `rte` alone, `rts` alone, and `rte` plus `rts` instead of skipping them as unknown fields.
`snapshotFramingSize` takes only `(ns, snapshot_id, row_count)` and preserves its exact byte count.
`writeSnapshotMeta` writes `live`, `decodeRefTableSnapshot` requires `lc`, and decoding rejects every `lc` value other than `live`.
`src/Disks/tests/gtest_cas_fold_seal_format.cpp:318` intentionally constructs the generation-6 `nsc` record and requires the generation-7 decoder to reject the marker-driven handshake.
The HEAD-before-GET pair is a protocol step and must not be removed as a cheap performance optimization.
HTTP 412 `Precondition Failed` is deterministic for conditional requests and must not be retried, even when an SDK classifies a non-AWS error body as retryable `UNKNOWN`.

The GCS conditional dialect maps `If-None-Match: *` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0`, maps numeric `If-Match` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: <generation>`, rejects non-numeric `If-Match`, and rejects conditional `CompleteMultipartUpload`.

The object-storage interface provides `removeObjectIfTokenMatches` for token-exact deletion and `copyObjectConditional` for write-once server-side copy with `If-None-Match: *`, both with fail-closed defaults.
`conditionalOpsUseGenerationTokens` and `isBucketVersioningEnabled` expose GCS generation-token and versioned-bucket capabilities so conditional operations can fail closed when unsupported.
`WriteBufferFromFileBase` exposes `getResultObjectETag`, and `WriteBufferFromFileDecorator` forwards it so a CAS writer can record the written incarnation token without a follow-up HEAD request.

A blob's identity H is a streaming, chunked cityHash128 computed incrementally via HashingWriteBuffer with block size DBMS_DEFAULT_HASHING_BLOCK_SIZE = 2048 as bytes are written, not a one-shot hash of a pre-existing buffer and not read from checksums.txt; the storage key is blobs/<H[:2]>/<H>.

Upload by placement: new content is written PUT If-None-Match:* (idempotent, dedup hit skips upload); cold reuse of an existing blob point-reads the object's per-hash .meta freshness state (Core/CasBlobMeta.h, MetaState{Clean,Condemned}) — condemned triggers resurrect with a fresh incarnation_tag, else the blob is reused as-is; this point-read replaced the old writer-side retire view.

The build writes a precommit binding to a /_precommits namespace shard before publish, giving GC visibility into in-flight blobs; the fold barrier holds the +1 edge until the manifest body is present. Publish is one CAS PUT to the ref shard updating refs[part_name] and appending {+, name, T} to the journal atomically; tokened deps are edge-protected (EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE) and not re-checked at promote, while non-tokened deps get a per-hash .meta point-read and copy-forward-if-condemned inline in the blob-revalidation loop.

CAS's condemned detection is a per-hash `.meta` point-read (`BlobMeta{version, state, condemn_round, size}` with `MetaState::Clean`/`Condemned`), not a writer-side retired-view cache; the earlier `Store::syncRetiredView`/`observed_gc_round`/`view_gate` machinery and the `MountLease.observed_gc_round` field are removed entirely. GC always writes a `Condemned` meta before ever deleting the body, so an absent meta reads exactly as live as a `Clean` one.

The writer consults the per-hash `.meta` with a single GET (`loadMeta`) only at `Build::observeAndAdmit` (dedup-hit/adopt path) and `Build::uploadFromSource` (fresh-upload/condemned-displacement path); a `Clean` or absent meta is adopted for free, a `Condemned` meta throws `ABORTED` so the caller re-uploads from source (INV-1) rather than reading the dying object.

EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE manifest-trust adoption: for a tokenless W-EVIDENCE dependency naming a blob referenced by a live committed source manifest, `Build::promote` trusts the durable manifest edge (`isTrustedAdopt`) with NO per-file HEAD/GET, because the source pins the blob (in-degree >= 1, GC cannot condemn it) and this build's own precommit edge is re-proved live at the promote owner-liveness gate before the trust fires; `copyForwardFromCondemned`/`isCopyForwardableTokenless` are deleted as a result.

On GCS's S3-compatible XML surface signed with sigv4, none of the conditional operations CAS needs are enforced (create-if-absent, conditional overwrite, and conditional delete are all silently ignored — a wrong-ETag DELETE on GCS S3-compat actually deletes the object); the same HMAC credential pair, signed instead with GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 over the GCS XML endpoint, enforces all of them via `x-goog-if-generation-match`.

The pluggable blob-hash Phase 1 design encodes the hash algorithm identifier directly in the blob's storage path (`blobs/<algo>/<shard>/<hex>`), records the pool's chosen algorithm in `PoolMeta`, and fail-close-validates that recorded algorithm against the disk's configured algorithm on every open, so an existing pool is never silently re-hashed under a different algorithm.

The content-hash algorithm (CityHash128) is an unversioned, unpinned pool contract (AD1-3): a future change to the hash algorithm would silently fork dedup and break relink, because nothing pins or versions which hash algorithm a pool's content-addressed keys were computed with.

`CasEnvelope` is a 70-byte little-endian core header (magic, writer_version, compatibility_version, hash_algo, flags, header_len, domain_id[16], incarnation_tag[16], build_id[16], header_hash[8]) followed by TLV extensions padded to a per-pool fixed `header_len`, so blob payloads always start at a constant offset for a constant-shift `locate`; `logical_size`/`logical_hash` core fields were dropped 2026-07-11 to let the header be built before the payload streams (S3-native staging).

`CasBlobMeta` (the `.meta` freshness sibling) is a fixed `CAMT`-magic codec with `BODY_LEN=22` (magic[4]+version[1]+state[1]+condemn_round[8 LE]+size[8 LE]); `version` must equal 1 and `state` must be Clean=0 or Condemned=1, else decode fail-closes.
Plain dedup adoption itself is free of `.meta` write cost (`CasBuild.cpp:337`); an earlier revision of the soak audit mislabeled the dedup-adoption class as carrying `.meta` write tags.
The envelope's `domain_id`, `incarnation_tag`, and `build_id` are excluded from `logical_hash`, allowing a new physical incarnation without changing the content address.
The incarnation tag is carried in the object body rather than provider metadata so changing it creates a new backend token without a metadata copy and remains portable across S3, GCS, and Azure.
The ETag fix makes `WriteBufferFromS3` return the `PutObject` or `CompleteMultipartUpload` response ETag, eliminating the head-after-put `HEAD`.

For tokenless evidence dependencies, `observeAndAdmit` reads and verifies the condemned object, wraps the payload with a fresh `incarnation_tag` and this build's `build_id`, and conditionally overwrites the observed token before admitting the new token.

Condemned-blob recreation uses the existing `Build::putBlob` cold-reuse rule on a retried build; the promote gate remains fail-closed with `ABORTED` because build-local sources are not retained at promote time.
GCS conditional semantics require a non-`x-amz` authentication dialect: GOOG4-HMAC or OAuth Bearer; `x-goog-*` headers cannot be mixed into sigv4 requests because GCS returns `ExcessHeaderValues`.
Build retains a parallel map of BlobSource objects for every putBlob hash, including streamed uploads and dedup-adopted blobs, because DepEntry is reassigned on adopt paths.
The tokened fix retains BlobSource in a parallel map for every putBlob hash, including dedup-adopted hashes, because later condemnation can affect an adopted incarnation too.
Build::promote keeps the outside-the-lock tokenless copy-forward pre-pass as a fast path and adds an in-closure backstop for condemnations visible only in the refreshed view.
The settled v3 blob layout keeps one key per hash and a minimal in-body 16-byte incarnation_tag plus payload; the manifest remains pure content and reads use a constant offset.
Freshness-meta v3 replaces writer-side RetireView retired-list downloads with per-hash .meta point-reads while leaving the exact-token body-delete core and read path unchanged.

An HTTP-attempt timeout is not the deadline for a complete logical CAS operation; CAS code owns retries, gates attempts on the local mount fence and remaining lease time, resolves uncertain writes from exact keys where permitted, and bounds retry budgets.
No protocol-significant CAS operation inherits an unexamined generic S3 retry policy.
Object-storage token handling is consolidated into `tokenForHead`, `tokenForList`, and `tokenMatches` so native ETag, GCS generation, and emulated list-token policies have one source of truth.

The shared S3 412 policy is consolidated into `S3::isPreconditionFailedError` and `S3Exception::isPreconditionFailed`, checking the HTTP response code first and canonical exception name/message as fallback.

Insert and merge uploads have different recovery behavior under a RustFS stall: an insert can re-stream from its still-live scratch file inside the query, while a merge failure discards the whole task and rebuilds without a durable object to adopt; proposed remedies are preserving staged merge results or using a size-proportional stream budget, with a circuit breaker as the outer safety limit.
Every persisted CAS format is converted to text, including `ref_log`, `ref_snap`, and the `blob_meta` sidecar; raw payload bytes are the only binary exception.
Wire structs such as `BlobMeta`, `RefLogTxn`, and `FoldSeal` move with their codecs into `Core/Formats/`, while protocol logic requiring a backend or layout remains in `Core/`.
`RefOwnerBinding` and `RefOwnerKind` are shared by the ref log and snapshot codecs in `Core/Formats/CasRefWireVocab.{h,cpp}` so peer codecs do not depend on one another.

The part manifest remains one object; its embedded `CARN` `RunKind::ManifestEntries` stream is replaced inside the same body by JSON entry lines and a trailer, with no separate object and no `CasRecordStreamFormat` reuse.
`ObjectKind`, `ProvenanceOp`, `Provenance`, and the slim `EnvelopeHeader` move with the envelope codec into `Core/Formats/CasBlobEnvelopeFormat`, while `CasEnvelope.{h,cpp}` are deleted.

The proposed `CasBlobUploader` extraction moves byte delivery such as `putBlob`, `observeAndAdmit`, `uploadFromSource`, HEAD-first handling, and staging promote/resurrect execution, while admit/adopt/resurrect choice, dependency recording, and the `promote` gate remain transaction state.

The CA branch of `DataPartStorageOnDiskBase::clonePart` creates one destination transaction, recursively streams every source file through non-autocommit `IDiskTransaction::writeFile`, and commits once.
Cross-disk CA part copying is sequential because the transaction's staging map is not mutex-guarded and MOVE is latency-insensitive; parallel copying is deferred optimization work.

The L2 fix copies every part file sequentially through one destination CA transaction and commits once, causing `publishStaging` and `PartWriteTxn` to upload deduplicated blobs, create one manifest, and publish one ref atomically.

Freshness-meta conditional writes must be routed through the shared `CasRequestController`, using controlled put-if-absent and controlled If-Match overwrite variants; transient errors must be absorbed inside the controlled call rather than swallowed as best-effort failures because stale meta state affects point readers.

Transient CAS write failures that are rerouted to the client use `NETWORK_ERROR` and a retry-later path, while terminal content conflicts such as `republishRef`'s unique-reference refusal remain `ABORTED`.

`CasJsonWriter` owns a `String`, appends inline, and supports whole-object assembly for bounded formats plus a reused line-scratch mode for streaming formats; it avoids `WriteBuffer` lifecycle overhead and per-record heap allocations.

`CasJsonWriter::stringValue` scans for control bytes, quotes, backslashes, and `0xE2`, bulk-appends safe runs, and preserves the canonical JSON escaping for `\\b`, `\\f`, `\\n`, `\\r`, `\\t`, `\\u00XX`, U+2028, U+2029, partial `0xE2` sequences, and unescaped `/`.
Per-write retry behavior is selected with the backend-neutral `ObjectStorageRetryProfile` token, whose values are `Default` and `SingleAttempt`.

The CAS-specific predicates `isMalformedRequestError`, `isEntityTooLargeError`, and `isAccessDeniedError` are moved to `S3Common` so CAS classification and `S3Exception::isRetryableError` share maintained error-name lists; `isRetryableError` itself is not changed.

`PartWriteTxn::uploadBlobDetached` is a side-effect-free upload primitive that returns value-only results and does not mutate transaction state; upload results are merged into each part's build serially after the join.
`RefOp::payload` and the related `RefPayloadUpdate` API are deleted under the pre-release no-compatibility policy; `SetPayload` becomes `SetPublishedAt` with wire word `set_published_at`.
The multi-commit design uses one dedicated CAS upload pool disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`; upload tasks return `DepEntry` values and merge them into `build->deps` only after joining.

`uploadBlobDetached` keeps conditional body/meta operations, freshness transition to `Clean`, condemned-object resurrection, dedup-cache operations, event emission, request accounting, and ProfileEvents inside each upload task so branch ordering is preserved.

The validator uses fixed 128-bit `XXH3_128` through `Primitives/CasXxh3Streamer.h`, not the pool's pluggable `blob_hash`, because it is a protocol validator that must compare consistently across disks.
Content-addressed encryption deduplication is scoped per encryption key, with key-local hash derivation.

The proposed `ch128ctx` blob hash is `cityHash128(content) ∥ xxh3_64(part_name, file_name) ∥ size`, a 256-bit slot-bound digest intended to prevent cross-slot adversarial deduplication while preserving same-slot retry and replica-write deduplication.
`Build::putBlob` was changed to stream the staged source instead of materializing it in a `String`, resolving the observed CA upload memory blow-up.

Incarnation identity is stored in the object body rather than provider metadata because metadata is write-once and requires copy operations, has an 8 KiB cap, and S3 ETags identify content rather than metadata.
`Cas::Store` remains responsible for protocol and object identity, including ref resolution, manifest validation, blob-location translation, and committed-ref mutation.
The v2 Payload family keeps CABL constant-offset ranged reads and replaces header_hash with header_crc32c in the guard slot while leaving payload bytes unchanged
v2 changes CasEnvelope.header_hash to header_crc32c at [86,90), with [90,94) as a zero u32, while keeping the 94-byte core
v3 drops cas_blob hash_algo, domain_id, header_hash, writer_version, logical_size, and logical_hash because they are redundant, unvalidated, replaced by ch and bld, or already absent from code

Blob identity uses an in-body incarnation tag and an exact backend token for deletion; generations are absent from object keys, so the `404 → LIST` degraded read path is unnecessary and Keeper is optional.
Immutable CAS content uses a binary hashed format and mutable hot-path objects use protobuf; JSON, pack objects, and the write-only build-heartbeat object were removed from the format design.

`fanOutBlobUploads` takes `ThreadPool &` explicitly so the same inputs can be run through a size-1 serial reference pool and a size-N fanned pool in one process; production passes `Cas::blobUploadPool()`.
The fan-out uses `ThreadName::UNKNOWN` rather than adding a CAS-specific enum value to shared `setThreadName.h`.

Serial-versus-fanned equivalence compares stable fields, logical payload, and backend metadata state rather than backend token values because concurrent fresh and resurrect uploads can mint tokens in nondeterministic order.
For CAS, `createHardLink`, mutable `moveFile`/`replaceFile`, and `moveDirectory` must be staged eagerly in transaction order; otherwise MergeTree can read the old state before commit.

A conditional PUT with a large body and `If-None-Match` or `If-Match` can be deterministically rejected with HTTP 412 before the body is accepted, so `Expect: 100-continue` should be used above a configured size threshold.

GCS XML API conditional writes require native GOOG4 signing and `x-goog-if-generation-match`; AWS `If-Match`/`If-None-Match` and SigV4 semantics are insufficient, and GCS may ignore conditional multipart completion.

The content-addressed `writeFile` implementation, including append read-modify-write, autocommit-inline versus content-blob selection, and the deferred-finalize lifetime pin, is moved from `DiskObjectStorageTransaction` into `ContentAddressedDiskTransaction`.
`ContentAddressedDiskTransaction` dispatches every staging operation directly to the metadata transaction in program order, including `writeFile`, `createHardLink`, and the `moveDirectory` re-key.

The manifest-trust adoption trade-off (D4 relink trust model, ordinary ReplicatedMergeTree interserver trust) means a genuinely-absent adopted blob is no longer caught at promote time — it becomes an fsck `dangling` finding instead of a promote `ABORTED`; this is verified unreachable in production by source-pin plus durable-edge, backed by an independent EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE consult and a per-test reachability proof. This also incidentally fixed the S13 soak-run-3 liveness brick where `republishRef -> promote ABORTED (condemned)` had left a table readonly forever.

The GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 signer was implemented as a sigv4 variant (renamed constants: `GOOG4` key prefix, `goog4_request` scope, `x-goog-date`/`x-goog-content-sha256` headers) plus a precondition-header mapping (`If-None-Match: *` -> `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0`; `If-Match: <etag>` -> `x-goog-if-generation-match: <generation>`) and token extraction from the `x-goog-generation` response header, letting the existing CAS S3 backend target GCS natively via a `http_client = gcs_hmac` opt-in and a `TokenType::Generation` token kind.
A dedup-cache hit does not skip the occupancy HEAD; it avoids the body PUT represented by `CasBlobBodyPutAvoided`.

Before the streaming fix, `Build::putBlob` could materialize a `BlobSource` into a `String`, producing about 384 MiB peak RSS for a 64 MiB blob upload; testing this risk requires blobs of at least 256 MiB or the `ci/full` scale.

The CA write path historically spilled an entire part to `disks/ca/cas_scratch` before S3 upload: a 24 GiB part used about 24 GiB scratch and a 100 GiB part used about 93 GiB, so a part larger than local scratch was unwritable despite bounded RSS.
A single INSERT into a 256-partition table can take about 10 seconds because each partition piece performs a separate CAS commit with manifest, ref, and blob round trips.

`CasJsonWriter` reduced representative `BM_EncodeRefLogTxn` latency from 753 ns to 333 ns by bulk-appending one record at a time, but the proposed <=3x memcpy-floor gate was not met because the validating encoder remained about 10.8x above the 30.7 ns raw-copy floor.
Bulk deletion is rejected for GC because `deleteExact` must preserve token-conditional safety and report `TokenMismatch` without deleting the object when the token is wrong.
The HEAD-before-GET pair remains a protocol step under the standing veto; the proposed cache removes whole redundant edges and therefore does not remove the HEAD from an edge that is still fetched.

S3 bulk `DeleteObjects` is rejected for `pending_deletes` because it provides no per-object precondition, while `deleteExact` is safety-critical and backends that ignore its condition are rejected by `Cas::Probe`.

Comparing hot-tier consolidation snapshots via bare `checksums.txt` equality was rejected because MergeTree checksums are `CityHash128`, a non-cryptographic hash that must not gate a decision to skip reading bytes; inode witnesses / borg-style filesystem-identity caches were also rejected as side state alien to the CA model, whose identity primitive is re-hashing.
The generation-8 snapshot byte golden still begins with `{"type":"cas_ref_snap","v":8}` and retains the same ordered `"lc":"live"` metadata field.
Out-of-band uploads under a staging prefix must be adopted through verified hash-then-publish copy-forward rather than trusted in place.
A CA write path can spill an entire 100 GiB merge to approximately 93 GiB of local scratch, so very large parts require streaming hash support or documented S3-native staging.
The format-freeze work for `B176` must review envelope TLV fields and make the streamed `gc/snap` codec preserve streaming, compression, and ordering semantics.

In the meta-descriptor raw-body plan, the absent-meta AND absent-body retry mechanism in putBlob's step (Task 3 step 5) is left as an open implementation choice between a sentinel value and a re-throw-ABORTED-and-retry approach; whichever is picked, putBlob and observeAndAdmitByMeta must stay consistent.
The manifest decode cache assumes the backend token uniquely determines content, but the capability probe does not currently test TOKEN⟹CONTENT; a weak recycled token could serve stale manifests.
Plain-object helpers casPutObject and casRemoveObject bypass CasRequestController and can retry beyond the lease-bounded retry discipline used by the ref lane.
The TOKEN⟹CONTENT contract is load-bearing for the manifest cache but is not verified by Cas::Probe.
suppress_destructive is recomputed independently in fold and runRegularRound, so a future anomaly append between those reads could make fold and deletion decisions diverge.
B140-dangle was caused by separately durable snapshot edges and `folded_cursor`; embedding the cursor in the snap codec makes trim and snap coverage co-durable.
B140-dangle is pinned by tests requiring a shared deduplicated blob to survive dropping only one of two live refs.
The S04/S04b under-count bug was fixed by replacing persisted integer in-degree with an idempotent source-edge set, making duplicate removals no-ops.
The resurrect-reupload orphan occurs when GC tracks a retired entry by hash only; settling the old token without re-condemning a replacement token can leave the replacement present forever.
B157 read-your-writes coherence increments `shard_write_seq[key]` before cache eviction and prevents a concurrent stale GET from re-caching an invalidated shard decode.

B115 was caused by `ReadBufferFromFileView` retaining a stale `file_offset_of_buffer_end` after remote `setReadUntilPosition` discarded its inner working buffer, which could produce duplicated and missing granules as wrong query results.

The implemented ref lane trusts a cold LIST as complete and enforces strict increase but not middle-log contiguity, so a missing middle log can be silently skipped; the v9 contiguous-chain design exists only in TLA+ models and plans.

Deleting and recreating `cas/refs/<ns>/<shard>` under the old path-keyed cursor creates an ABA hazard: a stale `folded_cursor` can skip journal versions 1 through K in the recreated shard, losing its edges.

Without a valid `gc/state` baseline, trimmed journals make a fresh GC interpret long-committed live blobs as zero-in-degree and mass-delete live data; this is fail-catastrophic rather than fail-closed.

The queue implementation needed identity-checked map-entry erasure because a slow waiter could otherwise erase a successor queue by key and create two leaders with conflicts; test counters also had to exclude bootstrap and mount-renewal `casPut` operations.
If GC fences a fresh lease before the adopt GET, the old `claimMount` and `claim` checks can resurrect a fenced incarnation under the same epoch, contradicting the terminal-incarnation rule.

A rejected `ALTER TABLE s19_src MOVE PARTITION 2 TO DISK 'default'` correctly raised `Code:479 UNKNOWN_DISK`, but two `CasRootCas` operations occurred before validation, so the move was not perfectly atomic even though fsck remained clean.
Build::promote must stop silently overwriting a committed ref, republishRef must make destination re-drives idempotent, and Build::abandon must retire build_seq only after precommit removal.
Promoting over a pre-existing committed ref can leave two live Committed bindings for one ref and later make dropRef remove only the new binding, creating owner↔refs divergence.
With gc_interval_sec=5, GC can condemn a freshly written blob in the putBlob→promote window and cause ordinary INSERT to fail with ABORTED at promote's blob revalidation.

Build::promote's prior fail-closed revalidation aborted on a condemned tokened leaf even though that leaf had a retained writer source; the existing copy-forward pre-pass intentionally handled only tokenless adoptEvidence leaves.
The tokenless race exists because the pre-pass observes retire-view round R while mutateShard may refresh the view to R′, making condemnations in (R,R′] visible only to the in-closure revalidation.

A `tombstone` meta is terminal: a writer must never CAS `tombstone` to `clean`, because GC may already have committed deletion of the unchanged-token body; the writer instead waits boundedly for the meta to become absent and then fresh-uploads, failing with `ABORTED` on exhaustion.
The deterministic GC-delete-versus-writer race must prove that after GC wins `condemned` to `tombstone`, a writer observes the tombstone and fails with `ABORTED` instead of un-tombstoning it.
A deposed leader can leave a durable stray-Clean meta over a still-`delete_pending` blob when `clearSparedMeta` completes before the leader loses the `gc/state` CAS.
Stray-Clean meta lets a writer reuse the condemned exact token, allowing a later pending `deleteExact` to delete the live reuse and violate `INV_NO_LOSS`.

A pre-existing `RunFileReader::seek` bug can skip an exact full key duplicated across a block boundary because it selects the last block with `min_key <= target`; the independent fix is to select the first block with `max_key >= target`.

Before the variable-length digest port, `CasGc.cpp` condemn-sweep and several `CasFsck.cpp` listing sites used `hexToU128` inside `catch(...) { continue; }`, silently classifying every SHA-256 blob as foreign and causing a permanent leak or false-clean fsck result.
A predecessor PUT that completes after successor recovery can create a late older-epoch log invisible to the successor and later snapshots; a missed `+1` edge is a data-loss class, not merely a leak.
Unconditional staging-to-blob copy is unsafe because the read path does not rehash bodies, so overwriting a live object can expose a torn or short body as valid data.
A dedup shortcut that adopts an existing blob after HEAD without the condemn check can reference a blob pending GC deletion and violate edge-before-observe, causing data loss.

The positive fail-closed CAS GC baseline guard remained untested at HEAD even though the guard survives at `CasGc.cpp:927`; the fresh-pool tests covered only the pass case and a different adopted-seal guard.
`RunFileReader::next` trusts an un-checksummed `record_count` from the block head and can index beyond the block payload, violating `CasRunFile`'s fail-closed corruption contract.

The EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE invariant in `Build::observeAndAdmit` was guarded only by `chassert(precommitted)`, so release builds could adopt an existing incarnation without durable precommit and watermark protection.
`dropRefBestEffort` silently swallows rollback failures; a correlated backend outage can leave a permanently live phantom ref because GC reclaims only unreferenced objects.

Before consolidation, `RetryStrategy` recognized HTTP 412 while `removeObjectIfTokenMatches` and `copyObjectConditional` used only exception name/message checks, missing stores such as RustFS that leave the exception name unparsed.

The `Build::promote` owner-liveness closure guard is a race-only defensive backstop: both legitimate removal paths, abandon and `dropNamespace` cancellation, satisfy `requireAlive` before the closure, while only a narrow promote-versus-`dropNamespace` race reaches the closure guard.
A S38 post-restart finding reported `txn_id 2-0 not strictly greater than greatest applied 2-MAX` after a seal `{2,MAX}`, indicating that sequence zero should not exist.
The `adoptEvidence` relink lifecycle exposure was tracked independently from the abandoned §5 optimization and required a separate investigation.
The fetch-by-relink residual requires a `stageManifest` stall across at least two GC folds, every replica dropping the part ref, and a deposed leader firing `deleteExact(h,t1)` after promote.
The planned §5 spare-heal transition reintroduced the removed `clearSparedMeta` behavior by clearing a tombstone while the blob retained condemn-time token `t1`.
A spare that clears a tombstone can advertise a blob as Clean at token `t1`, allowing a stale deposed-leader `deleteExact(h,t1)` to delete the live body.

The current fsck oracle assumes a snapshot ID is also a log ID and silently skips a recovery seal on that assumption, rather than reporting the skip as checked; and repeated per-held-namespace anchor/repair GETs on every folding round are rate-bounded only by the scheduler, with no cumulative bound or backoff.

SEC-4: a pool-write-capable party (or a corrupt/huge object) can place a valid-CRC, valid-framing but enormous shard or manifest directly in S3; decoders (`decodeRootShard`, `decodePartManifest`) validate magic/version/CRC/journal-integrity but a valid giant body still allocates on decode, causing OOM in readers and the GC folder (GC folds whole journals). SEC-5: key builders route through `checkNamespace`, `namespaceFileKey`, and `mountpointObjectKey`, which reject empty segments, the reserved `_files`/`_manifests`/`_precommits` names, `..`, leading/trailing `/`, and `//`, but `checkNamespace` itself does not reject a `..` segment; this is safe only because the backend is an object store with literal (non-normalized) keys, so a filesystem-backed or path-normalizing backend would be vulnerable to traversal. Recommendation: reject `..` in `checkNamespace` so the invariant does not silently depend on backend key semantics.

Risk register #13 (Med-Low, confirmed): `WriteSettings.h:36-63` adds six S3 knobs including `shared_ptr<const S3::Client> s3_client_override` to a hot, widely-included, copied-per-write struct, whose `operator==` compares the pointer — this creates refcount traffic on hot write paths, surprising equality semantics, and a wide recompile blast radius. Suggested action: measure; consider a narrower CA-path-only struct.

The claim that a rewritten CAS `fsck` oracle is "seal-aware" is overstated: current `fsck` discovers snapshots and logs solely via untrusted `LIST`, silently skips namespaces when expected evidence is unavailable, and has no `unchecked` term for a missing or pointer/seal-mismatched authority, so it could be implemented by special-casing synthetic snapshot IDs while still accepting a listed ghost as clean.

Fetch-by-relink has no retention pin: the sender is fire-and-forget and releases the source part while the receiver's `precommitAdd` edge-PUT can stall, so if the source part goes Outdated and GC completes at least two folds before the edge lands, the sender's blob is reclaimed while the receiver's build still promotes successfully, yielding a committed manifest naming a deleted blob discoverable only by fsck; this is the umbrella review's top blocker (risk score 85).

An explicit `<use_fake_transaction>true</use_fake_transaction>` on a `content_addressed` disk is silently honored, causing `createTransaction()` to return a per-file autocommit `FakeDiskTransaction` with no commit point and breaking atomic manifest/ref publish; proposed fix is to throw `BAD_ARGUMENTS` at registration when the key is explicitly true on a CAS disk.
A live ref must resolve through present keys; an absent key is a surfaced storage exception rather than a silent empty read (INV-NO-DANGLE).
CasRequestController::putIfAbsentControlled gates every attempt by the fence and remaining deadline, resolves uncertain writes by exact GET, and treats differing existing bytes as CORRUPTED_DATA.
Build::promote validates the manifest, checks the precommit owner, revalidates required blob leaves, and publishes the precommit-to-committed binding only after those checks.
GC must not delete an object while any session pin or committed reference names it, preserving `INV_NO_LOSS` and `INV_NO_DANGLE`.
Deterministic GC artifacts such as in-degree runs and fold seals must be byte-identical on collision, otherwise GC fails with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

A crash before the round CAS leaves the prior generation authoritative; the next pass reruns from a fresh attempt and previously issued exact-token deletes are idempotent through `NotFound` or `TokenMismatch`.
Source-edge activation is set union and removal is set difference, so refolding either operation is idempotent.
Any clamp anomaly sets `suppress_destructive` for the pass, preventing graduation and pending or exact-token deletes until a clamp-free pass.
A retired entry whose in-degree recovers above zero is spared even when it is already `delete_pending`.
If an exact delete reports `created_delete_marker = true`, GC throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` because versioning tombstones can violate `INV_NO_RETURN`.
A rebuild over trimmed journals fails closed with `CORRUPTED_DATA` when no healthy adopted baseline exists, rather than silently under-counting live edges.
GC ordering is biased toward over-counting: crashes may delay reclamation, but must never make GC under-count a live reference.
A point-in-time `HEAD -> 404` is not durable absence; unreadable bodies clamp the fold and any clamped pass suppresses destructive decisions.
Per-hash metadata is an advisory freshness point-read, not the blob lifetime linearization point; exactness remains with the in-body incarnation tag and exact-token body delete.
Backend tokens must satisfy `head(k).token == prior get(k).token` only when the bytes are unchanged; this contract makes token-based decoded-shard caching safe.
CA tests write objects through the same production codecs used by readers, so the fixtures exercise real format round trips rather than white-box state pokes.

The test suite scripts concurrency hazards through backend subclasses and does not use sleeps to reproduce races; only `gtest_cas_part_folder_access.cpp` and `gtest_cas_ref_writer.cpp` use real `std::thread`.

CA tests are single-process, single-threaded, and clock-free for GC scenarios; genuine concurrency correctness rests on backend primitives, TLA+ models, and integration or soak tests rather than gtests alone.

`CaIncarnationCore.tla` proves `INV_NO_DANGLE`, `INV_NO_LOSS`, `INV_NO_RETURN`, and `INV_JOURNAL_COVERAGE` across adversarial writers, GC leaders, split-brain, resurrection, overwrite, and trimming scenarios.
A writer publish gate must consult durable `deadTok[h]` as well as in-flight retired state; consulting only retired state can admit a physically dead token after deletion.
The build-root model proves that both structural build-root reachability and fail-closed commit are necessary to prevent adopted-blob dangles; either half alone is insufficient.
`CaB140DangleMerge.tla` proves that trim gating and storing the fold cursor with committed snap edges are jointly necessary and sufficient to prevent trim-before-durable dangles.

`CaGcAckFloorZombie.tla` proves that two-phase `delete_pending` is required when two leaders interleave: a deposed leader may execute only deletes justified by pending state published before its pass.
The safety floor must be latched no later than the fold cut; reading it after the cut could graduate over a commit invisible to that pass's in-degree view.

`CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore.tla` proves the root-local part-manifest invariants including no dangle, no loss, no return, journal coverage, single ownership, manifest-body validity, in-degree correspondence, and attempt-scoped visibility.
Only the adopted attempt's artifact may be consulted by GC decisions; a deposed leader's artifacts must remain reader-invisible.
A clamped GC pass may hold back a landed reference, but must declare the clamp and suppress graduation and pending deletes until a later clamp-free pass consumes the held reference.
`ca-fsck` classifies a live ref naming a missing object as `dangling`, which is an `INV-NO-LOSS` violation and the only hard reachability class.
A persistent `unaccounted` object outside the whole GC view is anomalous under INV-2, while an object created and dropped between rounds may be transiently `unaccounted`.
`ca-fsck` audits ref streams arithmetically using dense IDs `1..T` within `(namespace, writer_epoch)` and exact-key reads starting at `_ckpt.checkpoint`'s successor.
The GC safety assertion is `{preview deletes} ⊆ {ca-fsck unreachable}`.
Positive scenarios assert that `system.content_addressed_log` contains no `read_missing`, `dangling_access`, `corrupt_dangle`, `corrupt_decode`, `snap_journal_incoherent`, or `exception` events.
`readManifest` fails closed with `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` and `INV-NO-DANGLE` when a live ref names a missing manifest.
`readManifest` rejects a body whose self-described ref does not match the journal `ManifestRef` or whose `root_namespace_id` does not match the owning namespace with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

A live committed manifest ref structurally protects its referenced blobs from GC because the fold cannot mark them zero-in-degree, and deletion additionally waits through condemn and `delete_pending`.
The current CAS safety model assumes one-live-object semantics; versioned-bucket marker stacks and version-specific conditional behavior are unmodeled.

CAS failure handling is conservative: lost folds, stale snapshots, duplicated records, and crashed leaders can only postpone reclamation because in-degree is an idempotent set of source edges rather than a counter.

The CAS safety triad is no-dangle, no-loss, and no-return: live references resolve through present keys, deletion requires durable retirement and later zero reachability with the exact token, and a retired `(kind, hash, token)` cannot become a valid dependency again.
